comments.author: dfadler
comments.body:
🤖 **Claude:** Measured follow-up to the earlier findings comment on #2238 (which answered "did a width budget ever exist": no). This one adds numbers for the policy decision. Research only; no renderer code touched. Measured on `main` at 53fd3cbf, `renderMermaidASCII(source, { colorMode: 'none' })`, width = widest line in terminal columns (`displayWidth`). Scripts: `findings/measure-2238.ts`, `analyze-2238.ts`, `cli-outcomes-2238.ts`, `dump-2238.ts`, `xterm-2238.ts` in the agent worktree (not committed).

## Summary

- 175 samples in `packages/site/samples-data.ts`: **p50 44, p90 74, p95 81, max 206** columns. 12 exceed 80, 4 exceed 100, 2 exceed 120.
- Only **two outliers** (206 and 130) are far past any plausible limit; the other ten sit at 81-101.
- CLI compact retry rescues 4 of the 12 over 80. The rest are structural (or, for xychart/pie, untouched by padding).
- `--layout mermaid` does not help: it is flowchart-only and fell back to the standard renderer for the widest sample.
- A plain 80-column terminal wraps an over-wide diagram so every row is broken, even at only 85 columns. Markdown code blocks scroll instead.
- **Recommendation: keep unbounded as the default; width stays an explicit opt-in (what #2119 already is). Do not default `profile: 'markdown'` to 80.**

## 1. Width distribution

| | n | p50 | p90 | p95 | max | >80 | >100 | >120 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all samples, default spacing | 175 | 44 | 74 | 81 | 206 | 12 | 4 | 2 |
| same, `-x 1 -y 1 -p 0` (compact) | 175 | 38 | 66 | 78 | 138 | 8 | 2 | 2 |
| `gallery: true` subset | 72 | 48 | 80 | - | 206 | 7 | 3 | 2 |
| `profile: 'markdown'` | 175 | 44 | 74 | 81 | 206 | 12 | 4 | 2 |

`profile: 'markdown'` changed the width of **0 of 175** samples, so it is a glyph profile, not a width one (it would need a separate mechanism to constrain width).

Samples over 80 columns, widest first (compact = width at `-x 1 -y 1 -p 0`; TD = width with `direction: 'TD'`, flowcharts only):

| width | compact | TD | type | sample | why it is wide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 206 | 138 | 19 (but 117 rows) | graph LR | Twelve Core Flowchart Shapes | 12 nodes in one LR chain, 7 rows tall |
| 130 | 130 | - | xychart | XY: Numeric X-Axis | axis/plot scale, not spacing |
| 101 | 97 | - | sequence | Self-Messages with Notes | one column per participant plus labels |
| 101 | 86 | - | class | All 6 Relationship Types | boxes side by side, labels between |
| 97 | 95 | - | er | Attribute Comments | wide attribute comments |
| 85 | 74 | 90 | graph | System Architecture | subgraph nesting |
| 85 | 75 | 85 | graph | Decision Tree | fan-out |
| 84 | 84 | - | pie | Long Labels | legend label length |
| 81 | 81 | - | xychart | Bar and Line Overlay | plot scale |
| 81 | 81 | - | xychart | 12-Month Dataset | plot scale |
| 81 | 78 | - | sequence | Participant Types | participants |
| 81 | 54 | - | class | Cardinalities on Every Relationship Kind | cardinality labels |

Per type (first keyword, `graph` + `flowchart` merged; counts differ slightly from the earlier comment because this run is on newer `main` and groups differently):

| type | n | p50 | p90 | max | >80 | >120 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flowchart/graph | 55 | 39 | 70 | 206 | 3 | 1 |
| sequence | 21 | 46 | 80 | 101 | 2 | 0 |
| class | 29 | 32 | 72 | 101 | 2 | 0 |
| er | 20 | 19 | 60 | 97 | 1 | 0 |
| state | 8 | 25 | 60 | 60 | 0 | 0 |
| xychart | 10 | 66 | 81 | 130 | 3 | 1 |
| pie | 26 | 52 | 52 | 84 | 1 | 0 |
| architecture | 3 | 70 | 80 | 80 | 0 | 0 |
| C4 (3) | 3 | 38-65 | - | 65 | 0 | 0 |

Why: widths are driven by diagram content, not layout bugs. Flowchart LR chains and sequence participants grow linearly with node/participant count; xychart and pie width comes from the plot scale and legend labels, which spacing options do not touch.

## 2. What the CLI compact retry does today

`src/cli/render.ts`: with `-w N` (or `auto`), render once; if wider than N, retry once at `paddingX 1, paddingY 1, boxBorderPadding 0` (each only if tighter than what is in effect); keep the narrower result; if still wider, print the output anyway plus a stderr warning. Exit code is 0 either way.

Outcome across the 175 samples:

| `-w` | fits as-is | rescued by compact | still over |
|---|---|---|---|
| 80 | 163 | 4 | 8 |
| 100 | 171 | 2 | 2 |
| 120 | 173 | 0 | 2 |

Still over at 80: Twelve Shapes (206 to 138), Self-Messages (101 to 97), Class All 6 (101 to 86), ER Attribute Comments (97 to 95), XY Overlay (81), XY Numeric (130), XY 12-Month (81), Pie Long Labels (84). Compact narrows 124 of 175 samples, median saving 13%, and **never narrows xychart or pie** (4 of the 12). So compaction is a flowchart/class/sequence remedy only.

Running the real CLI (`tsx src/cli.ts render --ascii -w 80 <file>`) confirmed the pattern: Twelve Shapes prints `Warning: ... 138 columns ... exceeding --max-width of 80. Compact spacing ... was already applied`, exit 0; System Architecture and Decision Tree print the `Note: ... applied compact spacing automatically` line and fit (85 to 74 and 85 to 75).

Safety point for any default: compact **changes the output of 121 of the 163 samples that already fit in 80**. It is only safe as a retry on overflow, never as a default spacing, which is how both the CLI and #2119 use it.

## 3. How mermaid-style layout behaves for the widest samples

`renderMermaidASCIIWithLayout(..., layout: 'mermaid')` (default cap 120; `mermaid-wide` = no cap):

| sample | result |
|---|---|
| Twelve Shapes (206) | fell back to standard renderer: `unsupported (shape "asymmetric" ... "trapezoid" ... "trapezoid-alt")`; still 206 wide, same with `mermaid-wide` |
| XY Numeric (130), Sequence (101), Class (101), ER (97), Pie (84) | fell back: "not applicable to ... diagrams (flowcharts only)" |
| System Architecture (85) | fell back: `unsupported (subgraphs)` |
| Decision Tree (85) | **layout-faithful, 99 wide x 89 tall** (standard: 85 x 35) |

So for the widest samples it is a no-op, and where it does apply it traded 14 columns for 54 more rows. It is not a width remedy. Direction flip is the only lever that shrinks the 206-column chart (to 19 columns), but at 117 rows, and it makes System Architecture wider (85 to 90) and Decision Tree no narrower, so a flip cannot be applied blindly either (that is the mermaid-ascii#47 cascade in #335's scope notes).

## 4. What terminals and Markdown viewers do with overflow

- **Terminal (measured, xterm.js headless 6.0.0, 80 columns):** wraps. Twelve Shapes (7 logical rows, 206 wide) occupies 21 terminal rows. Decision Tree (85 wide, only 5 over) goes from 35 to **70 rows, all 35 logical rows wrapped**, because every row reaches past column 80. Class All 6 (101): 11 to 22 rows, all wrapped. A diagram that overshoots by a few columns is therefore unreadable, not just clipped. (Terminals with autowrap off, or `less -S`, would clip or scroll; not measured.)
- **GitHub-flavored Markdown code block:** scrolls horizontally. The published github-markdown-css sets `overflow: auto` on `.markdown-body pre` and no `white-space: pre-wrap` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sindresorhus/github-markdown-css/main/github-markdown.css, read via fetch). I did not render these in github.com itself or other viewers (VS Code preview, GitLab, Slack); treat as unverified beyond that stylesheet.
- **Consequence:** an 80-column budget matters for terminals (where overshoot is catastrophic) and much less for Markdown (where it costs a scrollbar). That argues for the caller choosing the limit, not the renderer baking one in.

## 5. Recommended policy

Choices: hard limit, soft limit, profile-based, unbounded.

**Default unbounded; width is an explicit, caller-chosen limit; no profile default.**

1. **Default unbounded.** 163 of 175 samples already fit 80; a default would only act on 12, and the remedies cannot fix most of them (rescue 4 at 80; XY/pie unaffected; flip is unreadable for the 206 case). A default limit would turn today's working-but-wide output into errors (hard) or ignored warnings (soft) for the diagrams where wide output is least bad.
2. **Opt-in limit = #2119 as written** (hard, throws `AsciiWidthError` with `actualWidth`, `compactApplied`). The data supports hard over soft for an *explicit* limit: the terminal measurement shows over-limit output is unusable, so the caller asked for a limit it cannot meet and should be told rather than receive a wrapped mess, and the library has no warning channel (the #2057 premise). It also shows who needs the error: at `maxWidth: 80`, 8 of 175 samples throw after compact (listed above), 2 at 100 and 2 at 120. Document that xychart and pie will throw whenever the limit is under their natural width, since compact cannot help them.
3. **No `profile: 'markdown'` width default** (matches #2119's maintainer decision of 2026-10-15; the profile changes 0 of 175 widths, and Markdown viewers scroll).
4. **Not recommended now:** soft limit (needs a new result shape or callback for little gain), and label-wrap / direction-flip cascade (flip made 2 of 3 measurable flowcharts no better and the third 117 rows tall).

### What it affects

- **#2119 (draft, blocked until 2026-11-09):** consistent, nothing to change. This data can go in its review as evidence that hard-throw-on-explicit-limit is the right shape. Its "unset output unchanged" proof matches the finding that compact must never be a default.
- **#2057 (open):** its body proposes a *soft* limit and a markdown-default of 80; #2119 closes it as hard with no default. This analysis supports the #2119 version; suggest the #2057 text be treated as superseded when #2119 merges.
- **#2011 (closed):** its width item ("markdown profile defaults to ~80") is answered no, with data above.
- **#335 / #382 / mermaid-ascii#47:** the cascade (wrap, flip) remains unbuilt. The numbers above are the evidence for leaving it unbuilt unless a user asks.
- **`--layout mermaid` (#2181/#2182):** its 120 default cap sits above 173 of 175 samples, which is consistent; its docs should say it is flowchart-only so users do not expect it to bound sequence/class/ER/xychart/pie.
- **#1522 / the ER stack that prompted #2238:** not a width problem (as in the previous comment); nothing here changes it.
- Docs: `-w` and the compact behavior are still absent from the per-diagram guides in `docs/diagrams.md`; a short "output width" note (distribution, `-w`, 80-column wrap behavior) would close that.

### Not checked

Real-PTY wrapping on macOS Terminal/iTerm/Windows Terminal (xterm.js model only); how github.com, VS Code, GitLab and Slack render a wide code block (only GitHub's published CSS read); the 100 `xychart-N` catalog cases; the MCP path; #1917 and #2076 (named in the issue, not read for this pass). Counts drift as samples are added (174 earlier, 175 now).

<details>
<summary>Per-sample data (all 175: default, compact, TD where applicable)</summary>

Raw JSON is in `findings/measure-2238.json` (fields `w` default width, `h` rows, `cw` compact width, `mdw` markdown profile width, `dirTD`/`dirLR` for flowcharts). Reproduce with `pnpm exec tsx findings/measure-2238.ts && pnpm exec tsx findings/analyze-2238.ts`.

</details>

title: ASCII ER layer order differs from Mermaid 12.3.0 (ELK) and forces a crossing
author: dfadler
body:
🤖 **Claude:** Split from #2630. The ASCII ER entity table landed there; this is the one parked entry left from it, `er-ascii-crossings-labels` (`parked: 'ascii-er'` in `demo/fork-fixes-data.ts`).

```mermaid
erDiagram
  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
  ORDER ||..o{ SHIPMENT : ships-via
  PRODUCT ||--o{ LINE_ITEM : includes
  PRODUCT ||..o{ REVIEW : receives
```

**Mermaid 12.3.0** (audit render, `oracle-out/er-ascii-crossings-labels.png`): top row `PRODUCT`, `ORDER`; bottom row `REVIEW`, `LINE_ITEM`, `SHIPMENT`; no crossing.

**Ours:** `ORDER`, `PRODUCT` / `LINE_ITEM`, `SHIPMENT`, `REVIEW`, with one `┼` where ORDER's run to LINE_ITEM crosses PRODUCT's stem.

## What was measured (not guessed)

- Mermaid 12.3.0 draws ER with ELK layered, not dagre. `getData()` hands dagre the same node and edge order we use, and `dagre-d3-es@7.0.14` on that graph gives our order, not Mermaid's (it keeps one crossing). A port of dagre's ordering therefore does not match either.
- This repo's ELK reproduction (`packages/elk-layout`, used by the SVG renderer) gives Mermaid's order. On 150 random layered ER graphs it picks a minimum-crossing order in 147; the parents' mean slot order we use is exact in 75, a dagre port in 86.
- Among equal-crossing orders (an order and its mirror, as here) ELK's choice is not derivable from the source graph. Picking the closest minimum-crossing order to ours matches ELK in 109 of 150 and would give `ORDER` first here, the mirror of Mermaid.
- Ordering the layers by crossings alone made this sample worse: the router (port and row assignment in `er-diagram.ts`) then drew two `┼` path crossings. The crossing is in the router, not only the order.

## Open decision

Either (a) make the sync ER path pick minimum-crossing orders and fix the router's port assignment (matches Mermaid whenever there is no tie), accepting that mirror-equivalent ties can differ from ELK; or (b) leave the entry parked and name the limit on the page. Exact parity needs ELK's tie-break, which only the async `layout: 'mermaid'` path (flowcharts today) can reach.

title: ASCII TD back edges + face port ordering (feedback-edge-sibling-order, longest-path-layering)
author: dfadler
body:
🤖 **Claude:** Part 2 of #2645 (TD diagonal back edges + port ordering + diamond bottom-slant ports). I could not un-park `ascii-feedback-edge-sibling-order` or `ascii-longest-path-layering` with a change local to `edge-routing.ts` / `port-offsets.ts`. No PR opened, nothing un-parked. Checked against the saved mermaid@12.3.0 oracle renders (a local 12.3.0 install was blocked by the package-age guard), starting from main 49d77469.

## ascii-longest-path-layering
- `buildFaceLaneRoute` rejects D->A: lane column `fc+3+slot` lands on node C, so `interiorCellsClearOfNodes` fails and it falls back to a right-face loop. Raising the lane base past nodes beside the column fixes that, but breaks 4 tests asserting the old shape (`ascii-back-edge-loop-1349` x2, `ascii-reciprocal-routing-1349`, `ascii-fan-out-exit-offsets-1308`).
- A<->C and A<->D are reciprocal diagonal pairs, gated out by `flowFanOut`'s reciprocal check. Lifting it plus Up->Down back edges gives crossings (`┼`), a canvas ~58 cols wide where the oracle is narrow, and a widened C. Needs port ordering, not just a gate.

## ascii-feedback-edge-sibling-order
- The subgraph-member gate in `flowFanOut` blocks the `No` leg. Lifting it routes `No` off the bottom, but Yes (straight) and No share the diamond's one vertex stem. A `staggerFanOuts` rule splitting opposite-bending branches onto the slants did nothing because `Yes` is a straight (anchored) member, and the path model has no jog to offset it.
- Dotted D->A with Up->Down routes on flow faces, but its bottom port on A sits left of the forward stem and crosses it; the oracle puts it right. That change moved 22 existing tests/snapshots.

## Suggested shape
A port-ordering pass for TD flow faces: assign each node face's ports in one sort (forward stems, back-edge ports, diamond slants by other-end x), then route. Per-edge shifts in `computePortShifts` cannot see the crossing.

**Measured**

The only tests that move are the four named in the brief: `ascii-back-edge-loop-1349` (x2), `ascii-reciprocal-routing-1349`, `ascii-fan-out-exit-offsets-1308`. The CLI dispatch tests also fail in a worktree run; I did not investigate, they do not touch ASCII.

With the lane past C, D->A, A->D and the x labels run as three nested lanes along the right edge, the canvas is about 70 columns, and A's bottom still has A->C / C->A on side faces. The oracle is about 15 columns of strokes: A's bottom takes six ports in three (out, in) pairs ordered B, C, D by the child's x.
- `ascii-longest-path-layering` also differs in columns, not only routing: oracle puts B | A over C | D (D right of C, A centred over C); the fork stacks A, B, D in one column with C beside B. Column placement is `grid.ts` placement, and moving it is not local to this entry.

title: Investigate Mermaid rank parity for cyclic subgraph exits
author: coderabbitai[bot]
body:
## Summary

Investigate Mermaid rank parity in the ASCII renderer for a graph with a subgraph exit and a return edge. The PR author reports that the difference from Mermaid also occurs on the merge base of PR #2796, so this is a follow-up rather than a confirmed regression introduced by that PR.

## Reproduction

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R
  T
  subgraph S
    A --> B
  end
  R --> X
  T --> A
  X --> B
  S --> X
```

Render the graph, then swap the declarations of `R` and `T` and render it again. The cycle crosses the cluster boundary: `S --> X --> B`, with `B` inside `S`.

The PR author reports the following results from headless Chromium with Mermaid 12.3.0 and the pinned 12.2.0 version:

- `R, T`: Mermaid places `X` beside `T`; the ASCII renderer does not match.
- `T, R`: Mermaid places `X` below `B`; the ASCII renderer matches.

The author reports that these results are the same before and after PR #2796. Mermaid is also declaration-order-dependent for this input; order dependence alone is not evidence of a mismatch.

## Follow-up

- Investigate cycle-breaking order in `computeMinLevels` in `packages/ascii-renderer/src/grid.ts` and establish how to match the relevant Mermaid behavior for both declaration orders.
- Add regression tests for both declaration orders using the agreed Mermaid parity expectations. Do not assume that both orders must produce identical ranks.
- Check that existing acyclic cluster-exit and feedback-edge behavior remains intact.

Requested by @dfadler.

PR: https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/2796
Review comment: https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/2796#discussion_r4498124277

title: ASCII: duplicate self-loops in a subgraph with its own direction override draw one hook (#2913 residual)
author: dfadler
body:
Split from #2913 (bullet 1 residual). Checked against mermaid@12.3.0 only (not checked on GitHub / mermaid.live).

A subgraph with its own `direction` override that differs from the diagram's still draws a loop on a member wrongly, single or duplicate. mermaid@12.3.0 (`scripts/lib/real-mermaid.ts`) honours the override and nests one hook per loop over the top of the node:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph S
        direction LR
        a --> b
        b --> b
        b --> b
    end
```

Ours (identical on main before and after the nested-subgraph-loop PR):

```
┌───────────────────┐
│         S         │
│                   │
│                   │
│ ┌───┐     ┌───┐   │
│ │   │     │   │   │
│ │ a ├────►│ b ├─┐ │
│ │   │     │   │ │ │
│ └───┘     └───┘ │ │
│             ▲   │ │
└─────────────┴───┴─┘
```

One hook out of the right face, crossing the frame's bottom wall; topology gate faces 2/6 and hooks 1/2 for this source. Cause: the loop nesting helpers in `grid.ts` (`nestedLoops`, `nestStride`, `nestInset`) and the margin pass read `graph.config.graphDirection`, not the frame's effective direction, so a TD grid carrying an LR frame sizes no top gutter. This is a renderer gap, not a target limit.

title: ASCII: cluster-exit labels share one row in mermaid (general-30); #1148 and #1331 say otherwise
author: dfadler
body:
Split from #3049 (general-30, State: Composite States, TD). Findings are in [this comment](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3049#issuecomment-6880613198). Checked against mermaid@12.3.0 headless (`scripts/lib/real-mermaid.ts`); not checked on GitHub or mermaid.live.

## Problem

mermaid puts `done` and `fail` on the same row (y 505), `done` left (x 80 vs 194). Ours has `fail` on the jog row under the cluster wall (row 46) and `done` pulled toward its target (row 55).

Both are cluster-exit edges, so `determineLabelLine` returns early for them. The row split comes from the gutter jog sitting just under the wall plus `pullTowardTarget` (`draw-arrows.ts`). mermaid also puts all labels of a staircase on one row: flowchart `S -->|one| X`, `|two| Y`, `|three| Z` are all at y=187.

## Decision

Two deliberate tests assert separate rows, which contradicts mermaid: `ascii-cluster-exit-anchoring-1148.test.ts` ("done and fail labels do not share a row") and `ascii-cluster-exit-staircase-1331.test.ts` ("every sibling's label sits on its own row"). Reversing them is the owner's call.

## Needed, if reversed

All exits' labels of a cluster share one row, the first jog row (straight and jogged alike). The gap under the wall shrinks: its 9 rows come from `widenClusterGutters` growing until the pulled `done` label clears, so they go away once the pull does. Re-baseline the cluster-exit samples (SVG and ASCII).

A 69-line prototype (`done` takes a jogged sibling's row, `draw-arrows.ts` only) fixes general-30's order and breaks 5 tests in 3 files (the sample's two snapshots plus those two), but with three exits it puts `two` on `three`'s row and leaves `one` apart, so it is neither distinct nor aligned. Moving the jog to mid-gap while dropping the pull broke 18 tests in 6 files, including an arrowhead with no line cell behind it (`ascii-lane-remaining-1826`).

## Done when

general-30 reads `done` then `fail` on one row, as mermaid@12.3.0 draws it, and #1148's and #1331's assertions are changed on purpose.

Refs #3049.

title: ASCII: place nodes by ELK's continuous cross offset, not a snapped slot
author: dfadler
body:
## Problem

`trackSlots` in `packages/ascii-renderer/src/grid.ts` snaps ELK's cross-axis centres to even cells (`2 * Math.round(((cross - origin) / unit) * 2)`, 50 units). Nodes less than about 25 units apart in ELK end up in one column, where mermaid@12.3.0 offsets them by half a box.

Reproduction (from #3147, BT flowchart): n1 and n5 share a column in the ASCII render. In mermaid@12.3.0, n5 sits about 0.4 box right of n1.

```mermaid
flowchart BT
  n2(["IwjRJr"])
  n1 -->|0| n3
  n6 -.->|0| n1
  n6 -.->|0| n3
  n5 -.->|0| n1
  n3 ---|ccc| n1
  n4 ==>|ccc| n6
  n6 -->|a| n5
  n4 --- n3
  n4 ==> n4
```

## What was tried (none shipped)

Checked on origin/main `c7ef08ddf`, over 83 flowchart/state gallery and fork-fix samples, ASCII drawn centres against mermaid@12.3.0 node centres (headless, `scripts/lib/real-mermaid.ts`).

| Rule | Samples moved | Closer | Farther | Topology gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global `round(x*4)` | 32 | 20 | 8 | arrowheads 400/401 |
| Fine cell only if no layer push occurs, else even | 28 | 20 | 5 | arrowheads 400/401, TD/BT 394/401 |
| Fine cell when an edge neighbour in another layer shares the even cell and fine cells differ by >=1 | 27 | 14 | 7 | arrowheads 400/401, TD/BT 394 |
| Same, fine cells differ by >=2 | 5 | 3 | 2 (incl. this sample) | arrowheads 401/401 |

A finer snap does not close the gap: an odd cell makes a narrow column, so n5 lands about 0.9 box from n1 (mermaid: about 0.4). The per-layer push (`next = at + 4`) also splits chains that mermaid keeps aligned.

## Proposal

Derive column widths from ELK's continuous cross offsets instead of snapping to slots. Gate: `scripts/ascii-topology.ts` stays 104/104 exact with arrowheads 401/401, and per-sample parity against mermaid@12.3.0 improves.

Related: #2645, #3147.

title: ASCII: parallel lanes out of a decision leave in the wrong order and cross (BT/TD, VW 38 Fp Zq)
author: dfadler
body:
Found in review of #3155. In `flowchart BT` with a decision and two pairs of parallel edges, the ASCII output has the `Zq` stroke crossing the `Fp` stroke. mermaid@12.3.0 does not cross them: its ports leave the decision in order VW, 38, Fp, Zq, each stroke rising beside its neighbour.

```mermaid
flowchart BT
  n1["F1"]
  n2["l2"]
  n3{"3D"}
  n3 -.->|VW| n2
  n3 ---|38| n2
  n3 -->|Fp| n1
  n3 ==>|Zq| n1
```

After #3155 the stray `+` and the overwritten text are gone, but the ports leave the decision as 38, VW, Zq, Fp: `Zq` starts left of `Fp` and its lane runs right across `Fp`'s vertical to reach `F1`'s right-hand arrow. The lanes of a parallel group are placed by `placeFace` (`port-offsets.ts`) in grid nesting order, not ELK's order along the face; for the lane ends in this source the hint order is not used (a first attempt to rank lane ends by `edgeHints` order did not change the result, because only `Fp`'s end reached that path). TD shows the same crossing.

title: ASCII LR/RL cluster-exit fans: wide labels rank the outer siblings' legs the other way from mermaid@12.3.0
author: dfadler
body:
Left over from the LR/RL cluster-exit fans of #2886 (mermaid@12.3.0, strict tie rule).

**Case:** a cluster with five labelled edges to one target and wide labels (`first label`, `second`, an unlabelled one, `fourth`, `fifth one`) plus `S --> U`, in `flowchart LR`.

**Real (mermaid@12.3.0), bend of each S->T edge:** 0.92, 0.84, 0.32, 0.24, 0.92 and 0.08 for `S --> U`. The fourth edge dips shallowly under T (its rise is the longest leg), where the grid draws it as a deep dip with the drop longest (0.82).

**Cause:** the grid follows the ELK hint, and our hint layout (`layoutFlowchartSync`) boxes edge labels at the drawn 11px, not mermaid's 16px, so with wide labels it ranks the fourth edge's legs the other way. The layout-only option `layoutEdgeLabelFontSize` fixes this for the ASCII provider's real-size layout, but the layout the hints are read from keeps the legacy sizes for graphs without a fan. The SVG layout has the same difference, see #3235.

**Also open, a target limit:** `Five Cluster Exit Siblings` LR edge #3 is a straight stroke in the grid. Real draws a 7px dogleg ([404,113] to [543,113], [543,120], [603,120], bend 0.70), under the half cell the grid can show.
